why:
The generated set in questions.json is biased toward keyword search. Its generator was told to name the specific people, examples and objects each chapter uses, because that specificity is what makes a question answerable from one chapter -- but it also hands BM25 the exact rare words it indexes on. So that set measures how well retrieval finds a question written by someone who has already read the chapter.

This set measures the opposite case, and it is the one the agent actually meets: a person describing their own life out loud, in their own words, using none of the chapter's vocabulary. No proper nouns, no ancient examples, no borrowed phrasing. If the vector side is earning its place in the hybrid, this is where it shows.

Written by hand rather than generated, because the whole point is that a model given the chapter cannot help borrowing its words. Gold labels are the chapter whose argument answers the question; where two chapters could serve, the more direct one is used.
